answers.q1: Cargo (Rust). Dependencies are fetched automatically on build, and there is no separate install step. To fetch them up front, run: cargo fetch --locked. To build, run: cargo build --workspace. The workspace requires Rust 1.96 or newer, edition 2024. On Ubuntu CI also runs ci/ubuntu-install-packages for system packages.
answers.q2: cargo test --workspace --features unstable-index. This is what CI runs first (with --verbose). CI also runs cargo test --workspace --features pcre2, and cargo test --workspace on cross targets. Optionally run ci/test-complete for the zsh completion tests.
answers.q3: cargo test --test integration regression. tests/regression.rs is not its own test target. It is a module of tests/tests.rs, which Cargo.toml declares as the 'integration' test, so the 'regression' filter selects that module's tests. Use cargo test --test integration regression:: for a strict module-path match. To match CI's feature set, add --features unstable-index or --features pcre2.
answers.q4: CI formatting check: cargo fmt --all --check. CI docs check: RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --no-deps --document-private-items --workspace. CI has no clippy step.
answers.q5: No committed generated or vendored source needs to be left alone. The man page (rg.1), the shell completions (rg.bash, rg.fish, _rg) and the deployment/ directory are produced by build.rs and are gitignored. target/ is build output. Cargo.lock should be updated by cargo, not by hand. benchsuite/runs/* holds recorded benchmark results and should be treated as read-only data. The shell completion templates under crates/core/flags/complete/ and the doc templates under crates/core/flags/doc/ are hand-maintained, so those are fine to edit.

q2.reason: Uses cargo test --workspace, which is correct, but adds --features unstable-index, a feature the truth does not mention as part of the CI command, so the main command is not exact.
